decisions: CSharp selects candidates before LLVM scheduling: only direct binding syntax, nonempty arrays without String/Struct literal elements, integral-number repeats with known count, nonempty Int dictionary geometry.
Static arrays do not require readonly-use analysis. Dynamic arrays and dictionaries require immutable bindings and every later owner use to be readonly; direct escaping Name use rejects promotion.
FindLastUseUnit returns the containing statement in the binding scope or the scope result, not the last lowered IR reference. Nested scope candidates are recursively collected.

BuildUnitPositions indexes nested scopes before their containing source unit, preserving expression evaluation order including additional call arguments and callback bodies. Source spans and LLVM schedule indexes are not an equivalent replacement.
Mutable owned containers add24-byte header candidates with scope-end occupancy and no automatic lifetime end; headers still consume the common4096 frame budget.

Async function frame plans are empty. Standard library inline plans are added as whole frames only if the remaining4096 budget fits, with slot offsets and first-source-identity allocation/lifetime ownership retained.

Native CoreEmitterState currently has no frame placement plan and its sole constructor is core_prepare. Existing fixed backing allocas are emitted separately in emitHoistedControlAllocas and are selected by syntax-only fixedArrayLiteralNeedsHeap.

Entry/function/control-region array consumers share ArrayStorageIdentity helpers but currently select heap or stack independently. Dynamic array and dictionary promotion, heap ownership cleanup, shared slot declarations and per-unit lifetime end emission all need the same prepared plan.

Private pure kernel14 and invalid guards6 passed CSharp/Native. This does not establish candidate collection, emitter consumption, original38-41 acceptance, source-phase closure, Stage gates or C742 closure.
nextImplementation: Implement one source-owned frame analysis before scheduler/emitter consumption. Retain explicit source-unit identity, binding mutability/readonly eligibility, nested frame boundaries and per-allocation lifetime sizes; no single-literal threshold patch or source-span substitution.
